question: Can scheduled Chat replace at least one bounded environment-sensitive compile/test-style outcome without executing an external compiler, build service, hosted runner, user command, or quota-bearing prover?

public_sources.title: Reproducible Builds — Definitions
public_sources.evidence: Reproducibility is defined over the same source code, build environment and build instructions; relevant environment attributes include dependencies, configuration flags and environment variables.

public_sources.title: SLSA v1.2 Build Provenance
public_sources.evidence: Provenance attests that a build platform produced artifacts through execution of a buildDefinition; builder identifies the platform that executed the invocation, while inputs/dependencies can be bound in the provenance.

public_sources.title: Translation validation — Pnueli, Siegel, Singerman (TACAS 1998)
public_sources.evidence: Translation validation checks each individual compiler/code-generator output against source semantics rather than proving the compiler globally; it presupposes that a target translation has been produced.

public_sources.title: Proof-carrying code — Necula (POPL 1997)
public_sources.evidence: PCC attaches an efficiently checkable proof/certificate to code so a receiver can check a property without trusting the producer.

public_sources.title: RISC Zero zkVM README
public_sources.evidence: Verification consumes a receipt, but first the code is compiled to a method and a host program runs/proves that method in the zkVM; therefore a fresh receipt still requires a prover/execution step.

candidate_matrix.reason: Reproducibility constrains repeated executions; it does not derive a fresh environment-sensitive output without performing the build. Source alone is explicitly insufficient because the build environment is part of the definition.

candidate_matrix.environment_binding: strong when complete provenance binds parameters/dependencies
candidate_matrix.reason: Strong for checking identity/provenance of an artifact that already exists, but SLSA provenance explicitly describes a build platform execution. Producing a new artifact/provenance still leaves an executor.

candidate_matrix.candidate: translation validation of externally produced target
candidate_matrix.reason: Validation can replace trust in a compiler run but does not remove the need to obtain the target translation in the first place.
The verifier is cheap relative to proving, but the official protocol still requires compiling a method and a host/prover executing it to produce a fresh receipt.

candidate_matrix.candidate: bounded proof-carrying finite evaluator executed symbolically by scheduled Chat
candidate_matrix.fresh_outcome_without_external_execution: YES within a fully specified finite semantics
candidate_matrix.integration_cost: low for tiny finite DSL; scales poorly
candidate_matrix.conflict_risk: low if certificate is content-addressed and premise-complete
candidate_matrix.reason: For a small formal semantics, Chat can derive both target and finite proof directly, then re-check every proof step. This replaces execution only where the complete semantics and environment premise fit inside an auditable finite certificate; it is not a general compiler substitute.

certificate_checker: require certificate explicitly contains the environment used by the derivation

changed_environment_negative.purpose: Directly falsifies any certificate that treats source text alone as sufficient for an environment-sensitive result.

missing_environment_negative.purpose: A proof/certificate that omits an environment-sensitive premise is incomplete even if the target happens to be correct for one environment.

result.what_it_replaces: one tiny compile/test-style environment-sensitive evaluation whose entire operational semantics and relevant environment can be represented as a finite derivation
what_it_does_not_replace: dynamic tests that interact with OS/network/filesystem/devices
compiler bugs outside the modeled semantics
fresh proof generation whose certificate itself requires a zkVM/SNARK/SMT/Coq execution service
result.acceptance_scope: Only the explicitly modeled finite semantics. Environment completeness is part of the certificate contract.

cross_field_revision: The strongest zero-quota route is not reproducibility or attestation alone but premise-complete proof-carrying evaluation for bounded semantics. Reproducibility/provenance become supporting identity and premise-binding layers; they cannot erase a fresh executor when the computation is not finitely derivable in Chat. This yields a transversal split: replace bounded deterministic execution with a certificate, and classify unmodeled/environmental execution as an unresolved child rather than a handoff.

frontier.action: Generalize the bounded certificate from one environment lookup to a small straight-line expression language with integer arithmetic, conditionals on declared build flags, and explicit dependency digests. Precommit a tiny checker grammar and test whether proof size/check complexity stays linear without hidden execution.

Search proof-producing/certifying compiler literature for compact certificates whose checker is substantially simpler than compilation, but reject any candidate where generating a fresh certificate still requires an unavailable external executor.

Test whether preexisting signed attestations plus a bounded proof layer can safely reuse already-produced artifacts without re-execution, while preserving exact environment/digest binding and zero-quota operation.
